question.knowledge_point: Identifying the Domain of a Hyperboloid
question.problem: Given the hyperboloid of two sheets $\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}=-1,$ find the domain of $z=z(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
From the hyperboloid equation, we make $z$ the subject as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =-1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+1 & =\frac{{z}^{2}}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{z}^{2}}{16} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+1 \\ {z}^{2} & =16(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+1) \\ z & =\pm 4\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

The square root is defined only for non-negative arguments. However, notice that for all $(x,y)\in {R}^{2},$ we have

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}+1\ge 0.
$$

Therefore, the domain of $z(x,y)$ is ${R}^{2}.$

These errors do not change the correct selections. Individually: q-164284 gives (y+6)^2=-15, so there are no real y-intercepts. q-35429 gives (x-2)^2=4, hence x=0,4. q-164303 has z=±4√(x²/4+y²/9+1), defined for every real pair. q-36465 requires (x-2)²+y²/4≥1. q-164376 sets z=0 to obtain x²-y²=1. q-74022 sets y=0 to obtain x²/3+z²/8=1. q-74913 has numerator 0 and denominator 2 at the limiting point. q-74910 gives √(3-1-1)=1. q-86868 simplifies to (x+1)/y and tends to 0. q-74919 simplifies to (x-y)/(x²+2) and tends to -1. q-129346 simplifies to √(x+y)+z and tends to 2. q-74960 simplifies to -(√x+y) and tends to -2. q-74903 has path limits 3/2 along y=x and 1/2 along y=-x, so its limit does not exist. q-129403 has path limits 1 along y=0 and 0 along y=x, so its limit does not exist. q-35927 gives x²/4=0, hence only the origin. q-164269 has vertex (0,3,-1) and its principal axis parallel to the x-axis, giving y=3 and z=-1.
